full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Abdul Aziz, .J: This Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties No. .1 and 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.4.95 passed by the learned subordinate Judge. First Court. Munshigonj in Title Appeal No. 21 of 1992 should not be set aside. 

 2. Opposite party Nos. I and 2 as plaintiff instituted Title suit No. 16 of 1990 against the petitioners and others for declaration of the impugned Kabalas as collusive, illegal and ineffective etc. and for cancellation of the same. The facts of the case of the plaintiff's-opposite party Nos. I and 2 in short inter-alia is that Abdul Ghani father of plaintiff No. 1 and husband of plaintiff No. 2 acquired title and possession in respect of suit land described in the schedule of the plaint measuring .25 decimals by purchase along with Ali Hossain father of defendant-petitioners who also acquired title and possession of the land measuring .81/2 decimals in the same plot by purchase that lather of plaintiff died leaving four suns including plaintiff No. 1 and 5 daughter and plaintiff No. 2 as wife who made amicable partition of the lands that the plaintiff' Nos. 2 got suit land measuring .25 decimals in plot No. 288 while defendants Nos. 5 to 7 who are also sons and daughter of Abdul Ghani and brothers and sisters of plaintiff' No. 1 got 15 decimals of land in plot No. 270 and 162 which they sold to Ali Hossain father of defendant-petitioners No. 1-4 about 37/38 years ago. The further case of the plaintiffs is that they purchased .7 decimals of land from the heirs of Jalal Box by kabala dated 8.6.88 and 24.7.77 and in this way the plaintiff's area in possession of the suit land as described in schedule 'Ka of the plaint acquiring title and possession by inheritance and by purchase and defendant No. 5 to 7 had no title and possession in the same but they sold the same secretly to defendant-petitioners No. 1-4 by registered kaalas dated 8.11.80 and 5.11.88 which the plaintiff' came to know from the reply of the petitioners tiled in a Criminal Case tiled against them by the plaintiffs on their throat to take possession of the suit land by force. The plaintiffs thereafter instituted the suit after taking certified copies of the said kabalas for declaration that the kabalas collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff's. The petitioners as defendant Nos. 1 to 4 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the averments of the plaintiffs made in the plaint contending that the plaintiff's have no cause of action to tile the suit that the suit is barred by the principle of waiver estoppels an acquiesce etc. The further case of the contesting defendant-petitioners is that defendant No. 5 to 7 namely-Nur Box Dewan. Md. Habibur Rahman Dewan and Sakina Khatun sons and daughter of Abdul Bhani brothers and sisters of plaintiffs No. 1 acquired right title and possession of the suit land along with other proportions and Nur Box Dwean sold .31/10 decimals and Habibur Rahman and Sakina sold 31/2 decimals of suit land to the petitioners by registered and since then they are possessing the suit land in their own right title and interest hence the suit is liable to he dismissed with coat. 

 3. Learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff's could not prove as to how much land each heirs of Abdul Ghani-including the plaintiffs and defendant No. 5 to 7 got and from which plot. that through that plaintiff alleged amicable partition that but they could not prove that defendant Nos. 5 to 7 had no right, title and possession in the suit land and their right and title was extinguished, and they failed to prove that the impugned Kabalas dated 8.11.80.and 3.11.88 are collusive, fabricated and illegal. Trial court also found possession of the suit land in favour of the defendant petitioners. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 and 2 being aggrieved preferred Title Appeal No. 21 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Munshiganj. learned Subordinate Judge. First Court who allowed the appeal and decreed the suit reversing the judgment and decree of the Trial Court directing the plaintiffs-appellants to pay advalorem court tee for the decreed prayed for by them. The appellate Court below allowed the appeal finding possession in favour of the plaintiffs and against defendant petitioners and finding the impugned kabalas ineffective illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff: Being aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and decree of the Appellate Court below the defendant No. 194 as petitioners obtained this Rule on an application under section 115(1) of the code of Civil procedure. 

 4. Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners took me through judgment and decrees of the Courts below and the evidence an materials on record of the case and submits that the learned subordinate Judge erred in law in finding that the impugned kabalas are illegal and not binding upon the p plaintiffs is based on no evidence and as such the judgment and decree of the appellate court is liable to be not aside. He submits that the appellate Court below erred in law in finding possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs and against the petitioner on misreading of evidence and also ignoring the facts that the plaintiff's could not prove that they acquired 25 decimals of land in the suit plot by amicable partition among the co-sharers after the death of their predecessor. He further submits that the appellate Court below having affirmed the finding of the trial court that the appellate court below having affirmed the finding of the trial court that plaintiffs could not prove amicable partition of the proportion left by their predecessor Abdul Gani and the saham acquired by and possessed each of his heirs in his proportion including the suit land, the appellate court judgment is liable to be set aside. He also strongly contended that there is no concurrent finding by the appellate court below from the evidence and materials on record that defendant No. 5 to 7 did not inherit and receive any 'sahan' in plot No. 288 which they sold to the petitioners by registered kabala on due consideration making over possession to them. Mr. Sheikh Abdul Awal, the learned Advocate also contended that there is nothing in the record to show that the impugned kabalas were collusive and fraudulent. He asserts that the title and interest of the vendors of the impugned kabalas having been legally and rightly transferred by them to the petitioners by registered kabalas followed by possession due consideration, the appellate court below has erred in law in decreeing to suit. Mr. Awal has referred a decision in the case of Abul Hossain Mollah & another-Vs-Khoteza Nessa Bibi & others reported in 46 D.L.R. page 310. 

 7. Plaintiffs case in short is that they got 23 decimals of land in plot No. 288 by amicable settlement among the hears left by their predecessor Abdul Gani. On the other hand the case of the contesting defendants petitioners is that their vender defendant NO. 3 to 7 also got saham in the suit plot and while in possession they sold the same to them. Admittedly both Abdul Gani the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 5-7 and All Hossain father of the petitioners (defendant No. 1-4) were the owners in possession along with others of the lands of the suit plot No. 288 by purchase. This is also admitted that the alleged amicable partition between the heirs of Abdul Gani predessor of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 5-7 allegedly took place 37/38 years ago. The impugned kabalas have not been marked as exhibit in the suit. The trial court found that the p.W.1 being the plaintiff No. 1 has admitted in his cross court in categorically that the land left by their predecessor was amicably partitioned 35 years ago but he could not say the amount/quantity of land got by each heirs nor mentioned in his plaint that the defendant No. 5-7 got their 'Sahan' in plot No. 150. The trial court also found that there is no mention in the plaint or in the evidence that how much land and in which plots heirs of the father of the plaintiff No. 1 got or that the defendant No. 5 to 7 did not get any property from any other plots except plot No. 238 or 270/262. Trial court also found that plaintiff No. 1 could not say as to how muchxiland his father left. On elaborate discussion and consideration of evidence of the P. Ws. the trial court specifically found that the plaintiffs could not prove no in the facts of the suit it could be believed that only plaintiffs got 18 decimals of land in suit plot No. 288 by amicable partition and defendant No. 5-7 got land in 238 and 270/262 only. These findings of the trial court have virtually been affirmed by the Appellate court below by its finding quoted below : 

 Both the courts below having thus concurrently found as above, the learned subordinate Judge has erred in law in decreeing the suit. 

 8. As regards possession of the suit land P.W.1 has stated that the amicable partition 35 years ago 15 years after the death of his father who left four sons, one daughter and a wife P.W.2 Sultan admitted that he has no land contiguous to the suit land in cross he stated that amicable settlement took place 40/45 years ago in his presence but he could not say how much of land received by each heir P. W. 3 had also no land to the surrounding of the suit land. He also could not say as how much of land the plaintiff No. 1 purchased. It may be mentioned that P.W.3 is the vagina (nephew) and P.W.3 is uncle-in-law of the plaintiff No. 1. The trial court on due consideration of evidence of the P. Ws. found specifically that it could not be believed that the plaintiffs alone possessed entire .25 decimals of land in suit plot. But the appellate court found possession of the plaintiff against the defendant without reversing the finding of the trial Court and seems to be on misreading without reversing the finding of the trial court and seems to be on misreading of the evidence of the P.Ws. It may be mentioned that no independent witness has been examined by the plaintiffs to prove his possession of the suit land. Trial Court also specifically found that the plaintiff could not prove that defendant Nos. 5-7 fraudulently executed and registered the deeds in favour of the petitioners nor the plaintiff's could prove that the kabalas were collusive. It is also found by the trial Court that all the D.Ws. have categorically deposed about the possession in favour of the defendant-petitioners. The appellate Court below decreed the suit finding that the impugned kabalas are illegal and not effective is not based on evidence nor the appellate Court below reversed the above finding of the trial court in arriving at his said finding. The finding of the trial court that the plaintiff failed to prove that the right, title, interest and possession of the defendants No. 5-7 had extinguished from the suit plot and failed to prove that the kabalas are collusive and without consideration, illegal and not binding on the plaintiff is based on due consideration of the evidence on record of the case which has not been reversed by the appellate court below. In that view of the matter the impugned judgment and decree passed by the appellate court below is not sustainable in law. 

 9. This admitted that defendant Nos. 5 to 7 transferred their title by registered kabalas such kabalas cannot be declared illegal and collusive in absence of any evidence to that effect and that the same was done fraudulently. Plaintiffs also could not prove by evidence to show kabalas were fabricated without consideration and collusive and no title passed through those kabals. A valid title transferred by registered kabalas cannot be cancelled in absence of any evidence that that the same is fraudulent fabricated without consideration and obtained by practicing fraud. 

 11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 25.4.95 and 28.4.95 respectively passed by the learned subordinate Judge, First Court, Munshiganj in Title Appeal No. 21 of 1992 is hereby set aside these dated 27.2.92 and 3.3.92 passed by the learned Assistant Judge. Tungibari Upazila in Title Suit No. 16 of 1990 is hereby affirmed.
